skills.name: Talking about violence and delinquency in school; reading a dialogue

note.text:
Text: A dialogue after class
Enow: Did you hear? Two Form Four boys were caught selling tablets behind the toilets.
Bih: Yes. Some students take those tablets or smoke cannabis because they think it makes them strong. It only makes them aggressive.
Enow: Last week one of them beat a younger boy who refused to give him money.
Bih: That is bullying. The victim should tell the discipline master or a teacher he trusts.
Enow: But he is afraid they will call him a coward.
Bih: Reporting violence is not cowardice. Our school has a counsellor, and the anti-drug club meets every Friday. If we keep quiet, the delinquents rule the school.

Words: delinquent (a young person who breaks the law), juvenile delinquency, drug abuse, bullying (hurting or frightening a weaker person again and again), a victim, aggressive, the discipline master, a counsellor, to report.

worked_example.problem: What does Bih advise the victim to do?
steps: Find what Bih says after “That is bullying.”
He should tell the discipline master or a teacher he trusts.
worked_example.answer: Tell the discipline master or a trusted teacher.

cards.idea: Bullying means hurting or frightening a weaker person again and again.
example: Taking a younger pupil's money by force is bullying.
Bih says reporting violence is not cowardice.

cards.idea: Victims and witnesses should report violence to adults they trust.
example: Tell the counsellor or the discipline master.

questions.prompt: Dialogue after class. Which statement is wrong?

right.text: Two Form Four boys were selling tablets.
A younger boy was beaten for refusing to give money.

wrong.text: Bih says drugs make students calm and strong.
wrong.explain: She says they make them aggressive.

wrong.text: The victim told the discipline master at once.
